mono-4218.d: Southern Magnolia (Magnolia grandiflora), a botanical study by Mary Vaux Walcott (1923) from the Smithsonian American Art Museum, printed as a one-ink halftone. Straight from a museum collection, in one ink.
mono-4218.c: Mary Vaux Walcott, Smithsonian American Art Museum

mono-4231.d: Design for a Printed Fabric, an ornament print (1820–40) from the Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum, its marks printed as one ink. History, worn lightly.

mono-4236.d: Lily, a botanical study by Mary Vaux Walcott (1875) from the Smithsonian American Art Museum, printed as a one-ink halftone. An archive piece, off the wall and onto a tee.
mono-4236.c: Mary Vaux Walcott, Smithsonian American Art Museum

mono-4276.d: Ornament Design, an ornament print by Alexis Peyrotte (1740–49) from the Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum, its marks printed as one ink. Looks like it came out of a portfolio.
mono-4276.c: Alexis Peyrotte, Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum

mono-4288.d: Country Road, a woodcut by Wanda Gág (1925) from the Smithsonian American Art Museum, its marks printed as one ink. In the public domain, now on cotton.
mono-4288.c: Wanda Gág, Smithsonian American Art Museum
